# Data {#sec-data} ## Sources | Need | Source | Access | |---|---|---| | Games, venue, neutral site, conference game, final score | ESPN scoreboard (`groups=80`, FBS) | Free, no key | | **Points by quarter** (Q1–Q4, OT) | ESPN scoreboard `linescores` | Free, no key | | Betting lines: spread, total, moneyline, open and close | CollegeFootballData `/lines` [@cfbd] | Free key, 3,000 calls/month | | Efficiency per team-game: plays, EPA/PPA, success rate, explosiveness, pass/rush splits | CFBD `/stats/game/advanced` | Same key | | Talent composite, returning production | CFBD `/talent`, `/player/returning` | Same key | | Transfer portal (2021+), recruiting classes, coach hire dates, preseason AP poll | CFBD `/player/portal`, `/recruiting/teams`, `/coaches`, `/rankings` (week 1) | Same key | : Data sources. {#tbl-sources} CFBD game ids are the same as ESPN's, so every table joins on `game_id`. Tables keyed by school name (advanced stats, talent, returning production) map to ids through **FBS teams only**, because some names repeat across divisions (there's more than one "Charlotte" and "Troy"). ## Ingestion and caching Both clients (`src/canes_cfb/espn.py`, `cfbd.py`) cache every raw response as JSON under `data/raw/`: - **ESPN:** a week whose games are all final is never downloaded again. Weeks with unfinished games are refreshed. - **CFBD:** one call per season per endpoint. Past seasons are never requested twice, and the current season is refreshed. A full rebuild of 2015–2026 costs ~60 calls. The data itself is **never committed** (`data/` is git-ignored, ~220 MB). It can be rebuilt from the notebooks in `00_data/`, and republishing ESPN/CFBD data in a public repository isn't appropriate. ## Validation Every check passes: 1. **One row per game.** `game_id` is unique across 10\,630 games (9\,764 completed). 2. **Quarters add up.** Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + OT equals the final score in every completed, full-length game (0 mismatches). 3. **FBS membership is right.** A team counts as FBS in a season if it plays 6+ games in that season's FBS scoreboard; FCS opponents appear only in their one or two games against FBS teams. The counts match reality (128 teams in 2015, 134 in 2024). 4. **Weather-shortened games are flagged.** 3 games ended before Q4 (for example, Kentucky vs Southern Miss in 2024, called for lightning). They have no quarter or half targets and are excluded from training. ::: {#cell-fig-fbs-teams .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![FBS teams per season, as identified from the scoreboard (2026 includes scheduled games).](data_files/figure-html/fig-fbs-teams-output-1.svg){#fig-fbs-teams} ::: ::: ## Coverage of lines and advanced stats ::: {#tbl-coverage .cell tbl-cap='Share of FBS-vs-FBS games with each data type, by season (%).' execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Two facts shape everything downstream: - **Closing lines cover every game**, so the closing line is always available as the benchmark. - **Opening lines only exist from 2021.** Anything trained *against the opener* has at most three seasons (2021–2023) before validation. That's why the market layer in @sec-modeling is deliberately tiny. Consensus lines are the **median across books** (ESPN Bet, DraftKings, Bovada in recent seasons). ## A data trap: swapped moneylines About 2.1% of FBS moneylines in 2021–2025 (mostly older providers) come with home and away **swapped**: the moneyline favorite is the spread underdog (for example, a team favored by 12 on the spread priced at +375). Left in, they made the model look like a gold mine on the moneyline (+12% to +42% ROI). `cfbd.clean_moneylines` now blanks any moneyline whose de-vigged probability is more than 15 points from what the closing spread implies; the honest moneyline result is −4.5% (@sec-reportcard).
